headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: xonsh can write and execute locally while PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images, creating medium prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests document/image content and xonsh can read/write the filesystem and run shell commands. If xonsh passes OCR outputs or source documents into prompts or scripts, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream instructions. No shared channel is explicit, so this is inferred from the documented surfaces rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF xonsh consumes PaddleOCR output from files or stdin without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF documents processed by PaddleOCR contain adversarial instructions and are later interpreted by xonsh scripts, the pathway exists.
mitigations: Sanitize OCR text before passing it to shell scripts.
Use a strict allowlist parser for any machine-readable OCR output.
Separate raw documents from executable working directories.
Add a manual review step before xonsh executes generated commands.
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags between OCR output and shell input.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while xonsh can read the filesystem and has broad network egress. A shared workspace would let xonsh access OCR inputs or outputs, and either agent could expose sensitive document contents through logs or network calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory tree, xonsh can read PaddleOCR inputs and outputs.
IF xonsh forwards file contents over network egress, document data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Place OCR inputs and outputs in separate directories.
Restrict xonsh network egress to approved destinations only.
Redact sensitive fields before OCR results are written to disk.
Review logs for accidental document content exposure.
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls or workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and spawn_subprocesses, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and may also write outputs through APIs. If both touch the same workspace, they can overwrite or race on files. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the conflict is plausible in default local workflows.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file overwrites or partial writes can occur.
IF xonsh launches concurrent subprocesses against PaddleOCR outputs, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Disable concurrent writes to shared paths.
Use atomic rename for generated files.
Check for existing files before writing new outputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can produce extracted text from documents, and xonsh can execute shell commands or scripts based on that output. If xonsh treats OCR text as authoritative, OCR mistakes or adversarial text can cascade into incorrect commands or data transformations. No verification step is documented, so the safer medium severity applies.
conditions: IF xonsh uses PaddleOCR output as command input without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF OCR output is copied into scripts or notebooks, downstream actions may be incorrect.
mitigations: Require human review before executing OCR-derived commands.
Validate OCR output against expected schemas.
Keep OCR output read-only until reviewed.
Log source document IDs alongside derived text.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and document-processing/data-engineering oriented, but neither declares regulated-data handling, residency, or retention commitments. The only concrete compliance issue visible is that PaddleOCR touches documents/images while xonsh can read local files and use broad egress, so a compliance gap is possible but not evidenced as a default breach. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through the shared workspace, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF xonsh is used to transmit OCR outputs to external services, policy review is required.
mitigations: Confirm data classification before processing.
Disable external transmission for regulated documents.
Set short retention on OCR artifacts.
Document where outputs are stored and who can access them.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention enforcement.
